clue.text: Society girl start to act, confronting likely early disaster

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society

indicators.note: the start of each following word is all that is wanted, so only opening letters of the next four words are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A debutante, nervous about acting on stage, is facing a probable early flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' applies to all four words that follow it, not just 'act'.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden and humiliating failure, which is a kind of disaster or fiasco.

clue.text: File design is so red

indicators.note: to design is to arrange or lay out afresh, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An office complaint that a folder's design is too red.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of documents about a person or subject, kept together as a file.

clue.text: The county, in short, makes money

definitions.text: The county, in short, makes money

parts.words: The county, in short, makes money
parts.note: surface reading: some county is briefly said to be profitable
setter's reading: the county's usual short name is a slang word for dollars

explanation.walkthrough: The county is normally abbreviated to Bucks, and bucks is slang for money. It is an English county just west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes an English county by its abbreviation, which happens to be a slang term for cash.

clue.text: Ninny is taken in by scoundrel engaged in hanky-panky

indicators.note: being taken in means being held inside, so the first word's synonym goes within the second's

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
noodle is an old word for a fool

explanation.surface: A fool is deceived by a rogue during some illicit romance.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, which is the playful sense of hanky-panky.

clue.text: Finally managed to capture antelope

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of a word, here the last word before the definition

parts.note: the closing letter of this word
to land something, like a job or a fish, is to manage to secure it

explanation.surface: Someone at last succeeded in catching an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: the most workable reading takes the last letter of 'capture' and puts it before LAND, from 'managed to (capture)'.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiralled horns, the biggest of its family.

clue.text: Plan shows Agadir wrongly situated by miles

indicators.note: letters placed wrongly need putting into a different order

parts.note: a Moroccan port, used for its letters
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A map shows the Moroccan city of Agadir in the wrong place, miles out.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawn plan or outline showing how something is arranged.

clue.text: Directors primarily vote for Blair's party to get casual working

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so just the opening letter of the preceding word

parts.note: opening letter
aye, also spelt ay, is a vote in favour
Tony Blair led the British Labour Party

explanation.surface: Company directors back the Labour Party to secure a casual-employment policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Day labour is work hired and paid by the day with no lasting contract, hence casual employment.

clue.text: A flower appeared

parts.note: taken as written
a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A bloom came into view.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is the past tense of arise, meaning came into being or emerged.

clue.text: Restoration involves return of monarch and ruling class

indicators.note: a return is a turning back, so the monarch's letters are written backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
the Establishment is the governing elite

explanation.surface: Bringing back a king, as in 1660, means the return of royalty and the old elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-establishment means setting something up again, which is what restoration of a former order is.

clue.text: Excited male can show restraint

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worked-up man is able to hold himself back.
explanation.definitionFit: A manacle is a metal shackle for the wrists, a physical restraint.

clue.text: Dr Roe caned my son violently in school once

indicators.note: violent treatment throws things about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent complains that the headmaster beat their boy at a school in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: Secondary moderns were British state schools for pupils who did not pass the eleven-plus exam, largely phased out from the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: This type of British secondary school mostly disappeared with comprehensive education, so it is a school of former times.

clue.text: Jones, the architect, is in Italy to work

definitions.note: the clue gives the surname; the answer is his first name

parts.note: taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
a machine that goes is working

explanation.surface: The famous architect Jones is off to Italy for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones was the 17th-century English architect who brought Palladian style from Italy, so the surface is historically apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect of the Queen's House at Greenwich was called Inigo Jones, so his forename completes the name.

clue.text: Face 'eated debate

parts.note: dial is slang for a face
heated means hectic, and the apostrophe shows the H is dropped, Cockney style

explanation.surface: A Cockney voice demands a heated argument face to face.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''eated' signals the dropped H, so the synonym hectic must lose its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is the art of reasoned argument between opposing views, a formal kind of debate.

clue.text: Role Tito Gobbi originally played in Verdi opera

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the singer's surname

parts.note: opening letter

explanation.surface: The baritone Tito Gobbi first sang a famous role in a Verdi opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Tito Gobbi was a celebrated Italian baritone who indeed sang the title role in this opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's 1851 opera about a hunchbacked court jester.

clue.text: Insipid and vulgar

definitions.meaning: second meaning: lacking good judgement in style

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both food with no flavour and behaviour or decor showing poor aesthetic judgement.

clue.text: In Hollywood, Betty drops Rex for Clark

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so a letter leaves the actress's name

parts.note: Betty Grable was a Hollywood pin-up star
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star leaves one co-star, Rex Harrison, for another, Clark.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was the Hollywood leading man of Gone with the Wind, so his surname goes with Clark.

clue.text: Strange-looking, eccentric, queer togs

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: togs are clothes; the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of someone's odd, outlandish outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotesque describes something comically or repulsively distorted in appearance.

clue.text: Penny designed tartan fabric

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
laid as in laid out, planned

explanation.surface: Someone called Penny created a tartan cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is woollen cloth woven in a checked tartan pattern.

clue.text: Perhaps Anne cut short Charles and Andrew?

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Anne is the Princess Royal, an example of the title

explanation.surface: Did Princess Anne cut her brothers dead?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals an example: Anne is one of a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles and Andrew are sons of Queen Elizabeth II and so are royal princes.

clue.text: Simon Rees disrupted lecture

indicators.note: disrupted things are thrown into disorder, so the names' letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Simon Rees heckled a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To sermonise is to preach or moralise at length, as one lectures someone verbally.

clue.text: Recruits listen in order to take shilling

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
s is the old abbreviation for a shilling, a pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: New soldiers are told to pay attention so they can take the King's shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the King's shilling was the old phrase for joining the British army, so the surface fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, recruits means signs people up for service, just as enlists does.

clue.text: Pretending to be at home from 3rd March to 4th June

parts.note: in means at home
since means from a stated time onward

indicators.note: an ordinal picks out a single position in the following word

parts.note: third letter

indicators.note: this ordinal also picks one position, in the month that follows it

parts.note: fourth letter

explanation.surface: Someone is only playing at being home for three months, March to June.
explanation.walkthrough: The dates are not dates: each ordinal picks a letter from the month after it, and 'from' is a synonym, not a range marker.
explanation.definitionFit: An insincere person is feigning feelings they do not have, which is pretending.

clue.text: Ena disfigured by six birthmarks

indicators.note: something disfigured has its shape spoiled, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A woman called Ena has six marks on her skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi is the plural of naevus, the medical term for a birthmark or mole.

clue.text: The revolutionary's extremely idealistic morality

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so the article's letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outer letters of the following word

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's moral code is extremely idealistic.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles, which is close to morality.

clue.text: Some recognise the lost girl

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the solution is a stretch of the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Some people recognise the missing girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a woman's first name, and crosswords commonly define names as girl or boy.

clue.text: Oriental Prime Minister often goes there at the weekend for recreation

parts.note: from China, in the Orient

parts.words: Prime Minister often goes there at the weekend
parts.note: the British Prime Minister's official country residence in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: An Eastern premier often goes to a weekend retreat to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country house, where weekends are often spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese chequers is a board game with marbles on a star-shaped board, a form of recreation.

clue.text: Type of agents working around the City

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the agents' word is wrapped about the other

parts.note: spies are secret agents at work
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A kind of secret agent operates around London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type of' looks like the definition, but 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort, as in 'a species of fraud'.

clue.text: Produces a secret mixture

indicators.note: a mixture blends things up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone makes up a covert recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To create is to make or bring something into being, the same as produce.
